title: Oceania capitals one of four · Palau, Pohnpei and the Marshalls
edition: Oceania capitals · Four regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Oceania capitals, episode one of four. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
We begin in the western Pacific, on three small island states: Palau, the Caroline Islands and the Marshall Islands.

states.name: Ngerulmud
lines: Ngerulmud stands on Babeldaob, the largest island of Palau, in the western Pacific a little north of the equator.
The capital only since 2006, and one of the least populous capitals in the world, with a few thousand people; its capitol building was modelled on the Capitol in Washington.
Remember Ngerulmud as Washington's little copy on Babeldaob, a capital of a few thousand people.

states.name: Palikir
lines: Palikir lies on the island of Pohnpei in the Caroline Islands, on a bay ringed by the mountains of the interior.
The capital of Micronesia since 1989, with only a few thousand people; on the same island stands Nan Madol, a city of stone islets built out over the water from the twelfth century.
Remember Palikir as the capital beside Nan Madol, the stone city on stilts in the lagoon.

states.name: Majuro
lines: Majuro lies on an atoll in the Marshall Islands, in the north Pacific near the equator, where the land is only a few metres above the sea.
The atoll is a ring of some sixty islets around a lagoon, and its one road runs about fifty kilometres along that ring.
Remember Majuro as a ring of sixty islets around a lagoon, with one road fifty kilometres long.

recap: Ngerulmud sits on Babeldaob, Palikir on Pohnpei, and Majuro on an atoll ring in the Marshalls.
Remember Washington's little copy on Babeldaob, the stone city of Nan Madol beside Palikir, and the sixty islets and one long road of Majuro.
